canada.title: Residents of this North York neighbourhood are demanding a traffic light after an eight-year-old girl was struck by a driver
canada.summary: Residents are calling for a traffic light to be installed at an intersection in North York where an eight-year-old girl was seriously injured last month, and the city says it is investigating now whether one is warranted.

canada.title: Funeral today for B.C. soldier killed in CFB Wainwright fire
canada.summary: VANCOUVER - The funeral for one of the four Canadian soldiers killed in a fire at a military base in Alberta is today in Vancouver.

canada.title: Regina councillor shared great replacement conspiracy theory with colleagues during mosque broadcast debate
canada.summary: Emails obtained by CBC News show internal city discussions about a Regina mosque's decision to broadcast the adhan, or Islamic call to prayer.

canada.title: Lawsuit alleges historic sex abuse by priest at Brandon residential school, Portage youth centre worker
canada.summary: A man suing the provincial and federal governments alleges he was sexually abused by a priest at a Brandon, Man., residential school nearly six decades ago, and that he suffered further abuse from a Portage la Prairie youth centre employee.

canada.title: Clinic offers 1-stop shop to help rural Manitobans access services from finding a home to filing taxes
canada.summary: A Steinbach clinic this week offered rural Manitobans help with a range of services, including getting ID, applying for disability and health benefits, and searching for housing and employment — all under one roof.

canada.title: This Nunavut student wants to be a nurse. Her community doesn’t offer the right courses
canada.summary: Faran Greenley, a high school student in in Cambridge Bay, Nunavut, wants to become a nurse. But her school doesn't offer the courses she need to apply. And neither do schools in 20 out 25 Nunavut communities.

canada.title: How N.L. plans to help seniors tackle the rising cost of living
canada.summary: Newfoundland and Labrador is planning to send payments to 130,000 seniors.

canada.title: Divers find long-lost WW II shipwreck headed for Saint John
canada.summary: The SS Cornwallis was on its way to Saint John when it was struck by a German torpedo in 1944 and hadn't been seen since. In July, a group of divers rounded off their seven-year-long expedition when they finally found her in the Gulf of Maine.

canada.title: Crisp air and golden sunsets: Enjoy these photos from around New Brunswick
canada.summary: This week's Your Lens features vibrant sunsets, fresh-picked apples and more fall foliage.

canada.title: Town of Lunenburg appealing housing project that is no longer planned
canada.summary: A proposed affordable housing project for Lunenburg has left the town in a court battle against an earlier design that is no longer happening.

canada.title: N.S. launches interactive atlas to guide health resources
canada.summary: Dalhousie University launched the Nova Scotia Health Atlas on Friday. The online, interactive map shows data related to many different health, environmental, social and demographic issues.

canada.title: Some bring hot tea, others spill it: Dawson City seniors getting healthy and having fun
canada.summary: Every Wednesday, a group of Dawson City seniors get together to hike the town's trails. It's a program organized by ElderActive and meant to get people together to socialize, and exercise during the winter months.

canada.title: Cell ‘dead zones’ in St. John’s west end causing havoc, missed medical appointments and more: residents
canada.summary: Fires that targeted telecommunications infrastructure in St. John’s back in the summer are still disrupting cell service and two west end residents want to see it resolved.

canada.title: Getting outdoors, and trying not to ‘let the old man in’
canada.summary: Physical and — perhaps to an even greater degree — mental health benefits of the great outdoors are immeasurable, writes Gord Follett.

canada.title: Injured Wainwright soldiers benefit from cutting-edge Canadian burn research
canada.summary: When news broke about the deadly training accident at CFB Wainwright that killed four soldiers and sent dozens more to hospital with severe burns, Véronique Moulin knew she had to help. She is on the front lines of research meant to help burn patients heal faster, with less pain and fewer scars.
